chunks: From him, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding

a man who struck a man with a stick upon his head, so his tongue became heavy. So he (peace be upon him) said: ‘There would be presented to him the letters of the alphabet, so whatever he pronounces eloquently from it, and whatever he cannot pronounce eloquently from it, the wergild would be (based) upon it, and these are twenty nine letters’.

key_terms.ثَقُلَ لِسَانُهُ: His tongue became heavy, indicating speech impediment or impairment
key_terms.حُرُوفُ الْمُعْجَمِ: The letters of the alphabet (specifically the 29 letters used in classical Arabic)
key_terms.دِيَة: Blood money or wergild, compensation paid for injury or death
key_terms.عَصًا: A stick or staff used as the instrument of injury

ai.seo_question: How is blood money calculated for speech impairment caused by a head injury in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the forensic methodology for calculating partial blood money (diyah) in cases of speech impairment caused by head trauma, a key topic in Shia jurisprudence regarding bodily injuries. By testing the victim's articulation of the twenty-nine letters of the Arabic alphabet, the Imam establishes a precise, quantifiable standard for compensation that reflects the severity of the functional loss. This approach underscores the Shia emphasis on objective evidence and proportional justice in civil liabilities.

en.hubeali: From him, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Abdullah Bin Sinan,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who struck a man with a stick upon his head, so his tongue became heavy. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There would be presented to him the letter of the alphabet, so whatever he pronounces eloquently from it, and whatever he cannot pronounce eloquently from it, the wergild would be (based) upon it, and these are twenty nine letters’.
